policy.note: Append-only audit registry. Every dismissal must be re-reviewed before nextRescanAt. CI fails once a record expires. Records are never edited to hide history; a superseded decision is appended as a new record.

dismissals.title: pg_graphql exposes user-owned tables to the authenticated role
dismissals.rationale: All 11 affected public tables (profiles, chats, messages, missions, memories, streaks, subscriptions, usage_daily, user_xp, xp_events, badges) are read directly by the authenticated frontend through PostgREST/pg_graphql. Every one has RLS enabled with owner-scoped policies on auth.uid() and no anon SELECT grant. Automated verification (scripts/verify-graphql-security.ts) executes real anon and authenticated GraphQL queries on every CI run and fails on any cross-user row. Revoking authenticated SELECT would break core product functionality; schema discoverability by an already-authenticated user is an accepted trade-off.
dismissals.evidence: scripts/verify-graphql-security.ts executed live anonymous GraphQL queries against every affected collection: HTTP 200 with zero rows returned and permission errors for user-owned collections; grants audited via SQL show no anon SELECT on any of the 11 tables and RLS enabled with auth.uid()-scoped policies on all of them.
